headline: Ice Cream/Milk/Sherbts: 579 of 2,319 scored households are expected to buy in the next 4 weeks (model estimate); no paid offer.

objective.statement: Within 13 weeks, find out whether a reminder brings back lapsing Ice Cream/Milk/Sherbts households, measured against a randomized no-message holdout, and decide whether to scale, change or stop.
objective.baseline: 444 lapsing households; model estimate of their chance of buying in the next 4 weeks is 27%.
objective.minimum_worthwhile_response: Act on a measured lift of at least 56.9 percentage points in the 4-week purchase rate (the break-even response under assumed economics).
objective.status: PROPOSED TARGET: a hurdle to test against, not a forecast

segmentation.meaning: shops often but has not bought the category in 12 weeks
bought earlier in the 12 weeks, nothing in the last 4
bought 1-2 times in 12 weeks, at least once in the last 4
buys the category in 3+ of the last 12 weeks

do_not_target_with_offers.why: They buy anyway: a discount gives margin away. Defend with recognition and cross-sell, no price offer.
Few baskets: no category action is worth its cost.

positioning.statement: Your usual Ice Cream/Milk/Sherbts, easy to find and easy to pick up again
positioning.status: HYPOTHESIS: to test with interviews and the holdout, not to publish

strategy_by_segment.what_we_do: Educational content and placement near related categories; no paid offer until a test shows response.
strategy_by_segment.kpi: first-time category buyers in 4 weeks, versus holdout

strategy_by_segment.what_we_do: Check availability, assortment and price versus competitors first (a reason to stop buying is often stock or range), then a reminder message.
strategy_by_segment.kpi: distinct buyers back within 4 weeks, versus a randomized no-message holdout

strategy_by_segment.what_we_do: General brand communication only; no category action.
strategy_by_segment.paid_offer_verdict: NOT EVALUATED (no paid action for this segment)

strategy_by_segment.what_we_do: Replenishment reminder and recipe or usage content in owned channels before any discount; confirm the product is in stock.
strategy_by_segment.kpi: share who buy again within 4 weeks

strategy_by_segment.what_we_do: No discount: these households buy anyway, so a coupon mostly gives margin away. Recognise loyalty and cross-sell a partner category.
strategy_by_segment.kpi: category purchase frequency and basket size; discount cost per buyer stays at zero

marketing_mix.Product: Confirm Ice Cream/Milk/Sherbts availability and range first
marketing_mix.Price: No blanket discount; a coupon only where the test shows response and the margin covers it
marketing_mix.Place: Digital owned channels and in-store placement near related categories
marketing_mix.Promotion: Reminder and content in owned channels; a paid coupon only after a randomized test

channels.role: fix reasons for lapsing first; place beside related categories

channels.channel: Content page for the learning questions (SEO/GEO)
channels.role: be recommended when shoppers are still choosing

budget.status: SCENARIO: assumed contact cost, redemption, coupon value and setup; panel households stand in for the company
budget.note: Paid items stay blocked until gates G2 and G4 pass; nothing is spent by this plan.

kpis.primary: incremental contribution per randomized eligible household after coupon and contact cost, 28 days

decision_rules.expand: 95% CI lower bound > 0 and all guardrails pass
decision_rules.stop: 95% CI upper bound < 0 or any guardrail fails
decision_rules.change: point estimate > 0 but CI includes 0 and guardrails pass

kpis.minimum_worthwhile_response: Act on a measured lift of at least 56.9 percentage points in the 4-week purchase rate (the break-even response under assumed economics).

discovery.status: OBSERVED answer log of a public analogue, not this retailer
discovery.reading: Shoppers who are still learning are not being recommended a store
discovery.action: Publish a factual page for the learning questions (how digital coupons work, store brand versus name brand); needs human approval; no sales effect is claimed

risks.risk: Discounting people who would buy anyway
risks.mitigation: No price offer to regular buyers; the coupon arm is limited to the target segment; the holdout shows the real response

risks.risk: Promoting a product that is out of stock
risks.mitigation: Stock confirmed before launch (gate G2) and a stock-out guardrail during the test
Only the consented pool is contacted (gate G2); opt-out rate is a stop condition

risks.risk: A misleading result from seasonality or contamination
risks.mitigation: Randomize inside the same weeks, keep the holdout clean, and read the interval, not the point estimate

Use it to order lists. Basis: on held-out weeks the model beats the simple repeat rule by 0.050 average precision (95% interval 0.045 to 0.056), history only. Success is judged on the holdout, not on the score

risks.risk: Assumed margin, cost or response are wrong
risks.mitigation: Finance confirms them in phase 1 and the break-even is recomputed before any scale-up

risks.risk: The discovery content has no proven sales effect
risks.mitigation: Track visibility in assistant answers only; do not claim sales
